forecasts.label: Interest payable

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Bury modelling shows housing account in deficit from Year 20 with Six Town Housing stock added
news_drafts.lead:
Bury Council's cabinet considered a paper on the closure of Six Town Housing, the company that manages the council's homes, on 4 November 2026. The paper says the current housing revenue account business plan goes into deficit in Year 20. It says that absorbing the company's housing stock into the plan as it now stands does not bring that date forward.

The housing revenue account is the separate, ring-fenced account for a council's own housing stock, paid for by rents. The paper says its modelling "does not show the HRA going into deficit earlier than is currently forecast". The modelling used the current business plan and the data held on Six Town Housing. The paper describes it as a high-level assessment built on several assumptions.

The paper concludes that the transfer is not expected to materially worsen the 30-year position of the housing revenue account. It says this depends on assumptions that are still to be tested in due diligence.
news_drafts.paper_title: Closure of Six Town Housing - stock options v2 - part a

news_drafts.headline: Bury's schools-funding deficit was £19.04m after 2024/25 target was missed; deadline now 2028/29
news_drafts.lead:
Bury Council did not clear its dedicated schools grant (DSG) deficit by the end of 2024/25, as it had agreed to do, according to an external audit progress report for the Audit Committee meeting on 19 October 2026. The DSG is the government grant that funds schools, and a deficit on it is an overspend, usually on support for children with special needs. Bury's stood at £19.04m on 31 March 2025 and is projected to reach £21.5m by 31 March 2026.

The target came from a "Safety Valve" agreement the council made with the Department for Education in 2021, under which it was to eliminate the deficit. The report, from the council's external auditor (the independent check on its accounts), says the council "could not eradicate its deficit by the end of 2024/25 target". An amendment to the council's DSG management plan has since been agreed with the department, with a new timeframe of the end of 2028/29.

The same report records an inspection of the borough's services for children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) by the inspectorate Ofsted. It concluded that "there are widespread and/or systemic failings leading to significant concerns about the experiences and outcomes of children and young people" with SEND, which the local area partnership "must address urgently".

news_drafts.headline: Bury faces £9.585m gap in 2027/28 budget after £10.747m of proposed savings
news_drafts.lead:
Bury Council's Cabinet on 14 October is presented with a refreshed medium-term financial strategy (MTFS, the council's multi-year plan setting expected spending against expected income). It shows a gap of £20.332m for 2027/28 before savings. The council proposes £10.747m of new savings, mainly by deleting vacant posts, redesigning services and changing policies. That leaves £9.585m, rising to a cumulative £17.508m by 2029/30.

The 2027/28 gap is £6.434m larger than the £13.898m set when the budget was approved in February 2026. Budget assumptions rose by £6.161m and expected funding fell by £0.273m. Demand and volume growth adds £4.084m, treasury and capital financing costs £3.094m, and the 6.4% rise in the Real Living Wage (the voluntary hourly pay rate set above the legal minimum) £1.482m. In-year budget monitoring (the check of spending against budget) forecasts a 2026/27 overspend of £5.691m, or 2.26% of the £252.135m net budget. Health and Adult Care accounts for £2.543m and Children and Young People £2.212m.

Money set aside to support the budget, the Budget Stabilisation Reserve, is forecast to fall from £15.599m at March 2026 to £5.977m at March 2027. That follows £3.977m of approved use this year and an estimated £5.691m to cover the overspend. The paper states: "The Council no longer has a sufficient Budget Stabilisation Reserve to fund the current budget gaps and therefore cannot rely upon reserves as a viable means of balancing future budgets."

findings.paper_title: Closure of Six Town Housing - stock options v2 - part a
findings.headline: The paper assumes additional management and responsive repair costs from the STH transfer will be marginal, citing economies of scale, with full financial due diligence still to come.
findings.detail: The paper says this is an initial and high-level assessment pending Cabinet approval, and that full due diligence on the financial impact will be carried out if the transfer is approved in principle. The 30-year stock condition projections rely on surveys for 84 of the 103 properties with some extrapolation.
findings.matters: The HRA case depends on the marginal-cost assumption, so a finance director would want to know if the costs prove higher once due diligence is complete.
findings.quote: any additional management and responsive repair costs will be marginal

findings.paper_title: Closure of Six Town Housing - stock options v2 - part a
findings.headline: The Sherbourne House lease, which runs to December 2031 for 12 tenants, is described as loss-making if taken into the HRA or general fund while used for supported housing.
findings.detail: The paper explains that the council would lose the higher exempt-accommodation Housing Benefit rate if it became landlord, leaving a shortfall against the lease rent that the council would have to subsidise. The preferred route is for another registered provider to take on the lease, with a fallback of rehousing the tenants through Adult Social Care.
findings.matters: A lease whose rent exceeds the benefit income it generates would be a recurring council subsidy, which a finance director elsewhere could compare against their own supported-housing exposures.
findings.quote: This means that the Sherbourne House lease would be a loss-making scheme if it were taken into the HRA or the general fund

findings.paper_title: Closure of Six Town Housing - stock options v2 - part a
findings.headline: Homes England Affordable Homes Grant to STH exceeded £3million, and the transfer needs Homes England approval for the grant responsibilities to pass to the council.
findings.detail: The grant was mainly for the Redbank Extra Care Scheme and several Mortgage Rescue properties. The paper says there are unlikely to be implications unless the council disposes of the assets on the open market, at which point grant recycling would have to be assessed.
findings.matters: Grant clawback or recycling conditions on a disposal could affect the value a council can realise from transferred assets, which is relevant to any council taking on housing grant-funded stock.

findings.paper_title: Closure of Six Town Housing - stock options v2 - part a
findings.headline: The STH loan balance of £2.691m as at 31 March 2026 is to be appropriated to the HRA as part of the transfer.
findings.detail: The paper says STH borrowed from the council to buy or build several assets. It assumes the remaining loan debt on STH's balance sheet will move into the HRA, and the modelling covers all remaining interest and principal on that debt.
findings.matters: Moving existing council debt into the HRA changes the HRA's debt position, which a finance director would need to reflect in the business plan and treasury figures.
findings.quote: the balance of outstanding loans in STH’s accounts was £2.691m

findings.paper_title: Closure of Six Town Housing - stock options v2 - part a
findings.headline: Bury's high-level modelling does not show the HRA going into deficit earlier than currently forecast after the STH transfer.
findings.detail: The paper states that the modelling used the current HRA Business Plan and the data held on STH. It concludes that the transfer is not expected to materially worsen the 30-year HRA position, but says this depends on assumptions that are still to be tested in due diligence.
findings.matters: The conclusion depends on assumptions about costs and data quality, so a finance director would need to know that the result is provisional.
findings.quote: does not show the HRA going into deficit earlier than is currently forecast
